comparisons.peer_summary: Commitments accounted for under the fair value option had a notional amount of $2.2 billion and $2.6 billion at December 31, 2024 and 2023, with cumulative net fair values of $144 million and $67 million classified in accrued expenses and other liabilities.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and Bank of America (BAC) disclose commitments accounted for under the fair value option. However, BAC reports a much larger notional amount ($2.2 billion in 2024) and reports cumulative net fair values classified in accrued expenses ($144 million liability), whereas GS reports a smaller notional amount ($568 million) and deems the fair value not material. BAC's disclosure also distinguishes between commercial and consumer commitments, noting it does not estimate fair value for consumer commitments due to cancellation rights, a distinction not made in the GS summary.

comparisons.peer_summary: As of December 31, 2024 and 2023, the contractual amount of lending-related commitments for which the fair value option was elected was $12.2 billion and $9.7 billion, respectively, with corresponding fair values of $50 million and $97 million.
comparisons.comparison: Both Goldman Sachs (GS) and JPMorgan Chase (JPM) disclose the contractual amounts of lending-related commitments for which the fair value option was elected. JPM reports significantly higher volumes ($12.2 billion in 2024) compared to GS ($568 million). Additionally, JPM reports material fair values ($50 million liability) for these commitments, whereas GS explicitly states that the related fair value of these lending commitments was not material. JPM's fair value exposure increased from 2023 ($97 million), while GS maintained immaterial status.
